title: Proposal: observe, activate, and close notifications via WebDriver BiDi
body:
### What is the issue with the Notifications API Standard?

## Summary

Add an "Automation" section to this standard that would let an automation client list shown notifications, observe them being shown and closed, and simulate a user activating or dismissing them. The commands and events would be defined as a WebDriver BiDi extension module, similar to how it is done in [Permissions](https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/#automation-webdriver-bidi) and [Web Bluetooth](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#automated-testing). A testdriver binding for WPT would follow.

w3c/webdriver-bidi#1199 continues here because it was was suggested to be moved to this project.

## Motivation

- **WPT coverage.** Activation and close behavior cannot be automated in tests today. The `click` and `close` events on `Notification` and the `notificationclick` and `notificationclose` service worker events are only covered by manual tests (e.g. `notifications/event-onclick-manual.https.html`), see web-platform-tests/wpt#51125. The newer navigation URL behavior in the activate steps has the same gap.
- **Web developers.** A flow such as "user clicks a notification, the service worker calls `clients.openWindow()` or `WindowClient.focus()`" cannot be tested end to end with Puppeteer, Playwright, or WebDriver without driving the OS notification center. A WebDriver BiDi module would dive these tools a cross-browser way to do it.

## Notification identity

Script has no way to identify a notification, and nothing in this standard requires one (point raised by @saschanaz in w3c/webdriver-bidi#1199). Automation still needs a way to say "activate *that* notification", so the proposal adds an identity that exists only for automation:

- Each notification in the list of notifications gets an **automation ID**, which is an opaque string assigned when it is appended to the list. IDs are unique and never reused.
- When a notification replaces another one with the same tag and origin, it keeps the ID of the one it replaces. This matches the show steps, which replace the old notification in the list of notifications in place. Clients see the replacement as another "shown" event for the same ID.
- The ID is not exposed to script and does not change any web-exposed behavior. It would be defined in the Automation section and could be omitted by user agents that do not implement automation.

## No platform presentation while automated

While notifications are automated for a user context, its notifications are not presented through the underlying notification platform. They are kept only in the user agent's list of notifications, and only the automation commands activate or dismiss them. This keeps tests deterministic and avoids races between the user and the automation client acting on the same notification. OS timeouts, Do Not Disturb settings and real user interaction cannot close or activate a notification in the middle of a test. For the same reason, the user agent does not apply the "close non-persistent notifications a couple of seconds after creation" behavior while automated.

The lifecycle:

- **Start.** Automation is turned on per user context. Notifications the platform showed before that stay with the platform and are not reported. Pages can still close them.
- **Stop.** When no session automates a user context any more, the notifications kept for it are closed the way the platform would close them. Non-persistent notifications get `close` events. Persistent ones get no `notificationclose`, because the user did not dismiss them.
- **Sharing.** Several sessions may automate the same user context. They share its notifications.

## Integration with the current algorithms

The proposal relies on existing hooks, with small changes:

- **Show:** the notification show steps (where the notification is appended to or replaces an entry in the list of notifications) emit a "shown" event and, while automated, skip platform presentation.
- **Activate:** the activate steps currently start with "when a notification, or one of its actions, is activated by the end user". They would be turned into a named algorithm that takes a notification and an optional action, so automation can invoke them directly. Activation through automation would also grant the same focus and window-opening allowances as a real activation (`clients.openWindow()`, `WindowClient.focus()`, `window.focus()` from `click`).
- **Close:** "handle close events" depends on whether the notification "was closed by the end user", which is currently implicit. The close steps would take that as an explicit flag, so that an automation-initiated dismissal fires `notificationclose`, and the "closed" event can report whether the user dismissed the notification.

## Proposed WebDriver BiDi module

The below follows the new `Notifications` domain that Chromium is implementing in its DevTools Protocol, adapted to WebDriver BiDi conventions.

```cddl
notifications.Notification = text   ; automation ID

notifications.NotificationInfo = {
  notification: notifications.Notification,
  userContext: browser.UserContext,
  origin: text,
  ? serviceWorkerScope: text,   ; persistent notifications only
  title: text,
  body: text,
  tag: text,
  dir: "auto" / "ltr" / "rtl",
  lang: text,
  ? icon: text,                 ; resolved URLs
  ? image: text,
  ? badge: text,
  actions: [* notifications.NotificationAction],
  vibrate: [* js-uint],
  renotify: bool,
  requireInteraction: bool,
  silent: bool / null,
  timestamp: js-uint,
}

notifications.NotificationAction = {
  action: text,
  title: text,
  ? icon: text,
}
```

Commands:

- **Turning automation on and off for user contexts.** This is the equivalent of CDP's `Notifications.enable` and `Notifications.disable`. See open question 1 for the shape.
- `notifications.getNotifications({ ?userContexts, ?origin, ?tag })` → `{ notifications: [* NotificationInfo] }`: the notifications currently kept for automated user contexts, filtered. A WebDriver BiDi subscription does not replay earlier events, so this lets a client that subscribes later, or that shares a user context with another session, find notifications that are already shown. This command is optional, we can drop it to keep the API surface minimal (see open question 4 below).
- `notifications.click({ notification, ?action })`: runs the activate steps. If several actions share the name, the first one is activated. Returns `no such notification` for an unknown ID. Returns `invalid argument` if `action` does not name one of the notification's actions, or is given for a non-persistent notification. The command completes once the page or service worker has handled the click event, or once the notification has been closed because the event could not be delivered.
- `notifications.close({ notification })`: runs the close steps as if the end user dismissed the notification. It completes once the close event has been handled or could not be delivered.

Events (subscribable globally or per user context, since persistent notifications are not tied to a browsing context):

- `notifications.notificationShown`: params are `NotificationInfo`. It also fires when a notification replaces another one, with the same ID.
- `notifications.notificationClosed`: params are `{ notification, reason: "dismissed" / "other" }`. `dismissed` means the user dismissed it, which under automation means `notifications.close`. `other` covers `Notification.close()`, the user agent closing it, and a click that could not be delivered.

The `no such notification` error code would be defined by this module.

## Open questions

1. **How automation is turned on.** One option is an explicit command per user context that mirrors CDP's enable/disable, e.g. `notifications.setAutomation({ enabled, ?userContexts })`. The other is to turn it on implicitly while a session is subscribed to `notifications` events for that user context. WebDriver BiDi generally avoids subscriptions with side effects, and here the side effect is large: notifications stop reaching the platform. So I lean towards the explicit command.
2. **Mapping a `Notification` object to its ID.** Should a script-side `Notification` (via `script.RemoteReference`) be resolvable to its automation ID? Unique tags plus the shown event cover most cases, but this would make some tests simpler.
3. **Navigation URLs.** The activate steps now navigate when the notification or action has a navigation URL. Should `NotificationInfo` and `NotificationAction` expose `navigate`? The Chromium CDP domain does not expose it yet.
4. **Is `getNotifications` needed?** The browser-level API Chromium exposes has no list command, so an implementation that bridges to it would have to track shown notifications that are not closed yet itself. Clients can do the same from the `notificationShown` and `notificationClosed` events if they subscribe before enabling automation. The command is a convenience, and we can leave it out of the first version to keep the API surface minimal.

Inline replies to text actions are out of scope: this standard does not define them, and Chromium's implementation does not support them for automation either.

## Implementer interest

- **Chromium:** will support automation, [work is in progress](https://crbug.com/576760752)
- **Gecko, WebKit:** feedback would be very welcome, particularly on whether you'd prefer this shape (WebDriver BiDi) or a test-only API, and on the identity and "closed by" changes above.
